chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Isa, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'My brothers and the sons of my uncle have constricted the house upon me and forced me out from it into another room, and if I were to speak to them, I could take what is in their hands.' He said to me, 'Be patient, for Allah will make a way of relief for you.'
He (the narrator) said, 'So I left, and a plague occurred in the year one hundred and thirty-one, so they all died, by Allah, and not one of them remained.'
He said, 'So I went out, and when I entered upon him, he said, 'What is the state of your family?' I said to him, 'They have died, by Allah, all of them, and not one of them remains.'

So he said, 'They were cut off due to what they did to you, and their disobedience to you, and their severing of the womb-relationship. Would you love that they remained (alive) and they constricted (life) upon you?' I said, 'Yes, by Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of relatives oppressing you and severing kinship ties according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the principle of *Sabr* (patience) in the face of familial oppression, linking the physical removal of kin to their spiritual and moral failings. The Imam’s confirmation that the plague was a divine retribution for *Qat' al-Rahim* (severing ties) and *Uquq* (disobedience/oppression) underscores the Shia emphasis on kinship rights as a covenant with God. The narrative serves as a practical example of how prolonged patience in minor trials can lead to significant relief, while unjust treatment of family invites divine justice.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, Usman Bin Isa, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘My brothers and the sons of my uncle have constricted the house upon me and thrown me out from it to (another) house, and were I to speak to them, I could take what is in their hands’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Be patient, for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would be Making a relief to be for you’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I left, and a plague occurred in the year one hundred and thirty one, so they (all died), by Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, all of them, and there did not remain (even) one from them.

So I went out, and when I came over to him<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘What is the state of your family?’ I said to him<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, ‘They have died, by Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, all of them. So there does not remain (even) one’.

So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘It is due to what they did with you and their disloyalty to you, and severing your relationship with a cutting off. Would you love it if they were to remain (alive) and they had constricted (life) upon you?’ I said, ‘Yes, by Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from certain individuals of our people who has said the following:

“Once I (Tsa) said to abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘My brothers and cousins have made life very difficult for me. They have forced me out of the house to another house. If I talk to them I am capable to take away what is in their hands.’ The Imam said, ‘Be patient. Allah will make a way out for you.’
I (the narrator) changed my mind. In the year one hundred thirty-one a plague came and they all died. No one of them was left alive.
I (the narrator) then went to see the Imam (a.s.) and he asked me, ‘How is the condition of your family?’ I said, ‘By Allah, all of them have died and not one is left alive.’

The Imam said, ‘It was because of their failing to maintain good relations with you, suspending you from their favors, withholding kindness from relatives and boycotting them. Do you love and wish that they remained alive even though they caused you difficulties?’ I said, ‘Yes, by Allah (I do wish so).”’
